title: NarraLeaf Studio plugin manifest (v2)
description: Mirrors Studio's validator at src/shared/utils/pluginManifest.ts. Editor tooling only — scripts/validate.mjs is authoritative.

manifestVersion.description: Must be exactly 2. Studio hard-rejects v1.

id.description: Namespaced lowercase id, e.g. publisher.plugin-name. The plugin directory must be named after it.

icon.description: Package-relative thumbnail shown beside the plugin in Studio's Launcher list. Must be square, at most 512x512 and at least 64x64, at most 512 KB, and .png/.webp/.jpg/.jpeg (no SVG, no GIF). The file must also be copied into dist/ by the build script — scripts/validate.mjs checks all of this.

entries.description: At least one target. Each value is a prebundled ESM file relative to the package root.

contributes.description: Every type the plugin registers. Undeclared registrations throw at load.

blueprintNodes.description: Blueprint node types, each prefixed with the plugin id.

widgets.description: Widget types, each prefixed with the plugin id.

runtimeData.description: Storage namespaces the plugin owns, each prefixed with the plugin id.

tests.description: Tests the plugin adds to Run > Test, each prefixed with the plugin id. Alone among the code-backed contributions this asks for nothing at install: a test runs only because the author opened the dialog and started it, and what it may reach while running is gated by its own requires.

locales.description: Translations the plugin ships. A code declared twice is refused rather than one copy silently winning.

runtimeCapabilities.description: Capability domains the runtime entry may reach. Closed list, so a typo fails validation rather than reading as "asked for nothing". Each becomes an install permission, which is why declaring one without a runtime entry is refused: it would ask the user to approve something nothing can use.

sidecars.description: Native child processes shipped inside the author's game. Requires a runtime entry, for the reason runtimeCapabilities does.

buildDependencies.description: Binaries fetched at build time and packaged into the game, for redistributables the plugin may not commit itself.

buildConfig.description: Values the author fills in before a build can ship. Keys carry no plugin-id prefix — the store is already per plugin — and must be unique within it.

externalLinks.description: Address patterns the plugin may hand to the player's browser or platform handler. Requires a runtime entry. The whole list becomes one install permission the author reads verbatim, so a pattern that could never match would be approved as a power and then be none.

permissions.description: Shown to the user at install time. Request the minimum. Only filesystem and api are written here: runtime, sidecar, buildDependency and externalLink are derived from contributes and refused when hand-written, which is what keeps the prompt and the plugin's real reach from drifting apart.

relativeEntry.description: Relative path inside the package. No absolute paths, no parent traversal.

code.description: BCP-47-ish: primary subtag plus optional hyphen-joined subtags.

targets.description: Desktop only: the web has no process to spawn and the mobile shells are WebViews, so a binary keyed to them could never run.

include.description: Every file this platform ships, the entry among them. A dep:<buildDependencyId>/<path> item is served by a declared build dependency instead of the package.

sha256.description: One digest per package-relative include, and none for a file the target does not ship. dep: includes are pinned by the dependency's own digest.

id.description: Prefixed with the plugin id. Sidecar dep: includes resolve against it.

buildDependencyTarget.description: A zip maps archive paths through files; archive "none" downloads a single file and names it with fileName.

url.description: https only. The digest would catch swapped bytes, but the failure mode should be "cannot be attacked" rather than "attack detected after downloading it".

files.description: Path inside the archive, mapped to a path inside the dependency directory.

label.description: What the author sees. A blank one produces a field nothing on screen identifies.

type.description: A secret is stored on the author's machine, not in the project.

platforms.description: Absent for every platform. An empty list is refused rather than read as "every platform": it is a field that applies nowhere, so nothing would ever ask for it.

externalLinkPattern.description: Absolute and naming a scheme, carrying no credentials, using * only as a whole leading host label or as the entire host. javascript:, data: and vbscript: are not addresses at all — handing one to the platform opener is how "open a link" becomes "run this" — and file: opens whatever handler the file is registered to, which for an executable is the same thing. The parts of this a pattern cannot express are checked by scripts/validate.mjs.
